history.sg_progress: The Administration will continue its efforts to manage the catering operation with the aim of reducing losses to the extent possible. Historically, all cafeteria operations lose money, while catering events generate profits. The Administration continuously monitors demand for food services and will adjust the number of operating cafeterias accordingly. The United Nations Postal Administration has been taking steps to reduce losses and will continue to do so by expanding sales and maintaining, if not reducing, costs. The Postal Administration operations and revenue-generating capability are currently being reviewed and the findings and recommendations are expected to be available by the end of 2023. Currently, garage operations at United Nations Headquarters generate sufficient income to cover expenses. It should be noted, however, that two external factors that are beyond the direct control of the Administration may affect this positive situation and future revenue-generating abilities. The first factor is the decision of the General Assembly in paragraph 63 of its resolution 77/262 to maintain garage rates at their current level and not introduce any changes in the garage operations policies. This limits the Administration’s ability to make any future rate adjustments in accordance with the prevailing economic situation in a timely manner, as it would require a request to the Assembly to adjust rates. The second factor is the expected implementation of congestion pricing in New York City, beginning as early as spring 2024, which would levy a daily toll on vehicles driving into Manhattan below 60th street. The additional cost, when combined with garage fees, may prove too costly to many garage users and therefore reduce demand for permits, which is the main source of revenue.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration request the Department of Operational Support, the Department of Global Communications and other responsible entities to continue to review their revenue-producing activities and take appropriate measures to minimize losses to avoid potential financial burden on Member States.
history.administration_response: The Administration continues its catering activities at United Nations Headquarters to offset the past losses of catering operations. A table with monthly catering financial results has been provided. Five of seven cafes are currently open and are being monitored by the Administration. The United Nations Postal Administration has been taking steps to reduce losses and will continue to do so by expanding sales and maintaining, if not reducing, costs. The Postal Administration continues to progress towards profitability despite the challenges it faces in relation to declining philatelic markets and aging of its core customers group. In an effort to adjust its operation to meet those market changes, the Postal Administration has engaged a consulting company to review its operations and revenue-generating capability. In addition, the Postal Administration is working towards replacing its legacy sales system and website with a more integrated and technologically advanced system. With the help of the Office of Information and Communications Technology, the Postal Administration has successfully launched two series of United Nations Crypto Stamps, which consist of physical stamps and their unique digital twins developed using blockchain technology for which customer response has been positive. The Administration requests the Board to consider the efforts taken to minimize the losses in revenue-producing activities and close the recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the revenue from tours and bookstore has increased remarkably in 2023, the Board consider this recommendation to be implemented.
